entities.summary: Henry IV of Castile, nicknamed the Impotent, was King of Castile and León and the last of the weak late-medieval kings of Castile and León. Born into the powerful Trastámara dynasty, Henry IV ascended to the throne in 1464 after the death of his half-brother, John II. His reign, which lasted until his death in 1474, was marked by a series of power struggles with the nobles and the clergy. As the nobles gained more power, the nation became less centralized, and Henry IV's inability to assert his authority led to a decline in the kingdom's strength. Henry IV's reign also saw the rise of the powerful Duke of Aragon, who would eventually play a key role in the unification of Spain. Despite his weakness, Henry IV played a crucial role in the development of the Spanish language and culture, and his reign marked the beginning of a new era in Castilian history. Henry IV died on December 20, 1474, at the age of 50, and his legacy was marked by the continued struggle for power between the nobles and the monarchy.
